Usage

Exact signed distance field of a finite-length cylinder (flat caps at both ends) (negative inside, positive outside).

Split into the axial distance t and the radius r from the axis; with q = (r - radius, |t| - height/2), outside = ‖max(q, 0)‖, inside = min(max(q), 0), sdf = outside + inside. This applies the same Quilez-style construction as box_sdf to the "2-D cross-section of (radius, axis)", and gives the true Euclidean distance to the side, the caps and the corners (rims) alike.

Arguments and validation (ValueError):

• grid: float array (..., 3) whose last axis is 3.

• center: the centre of the cylinder (the centroid, not an end face; 3 elements).

• axis: axis direction (3 elements; zero vector and NaN are rejected; length is normalised automatically).

• radius: scalar radius, nominally > 0 (0 is the axis line itself; negative is rejected).

• height: scalar total length (±height/2 from center; negative is rejected).

Return value: float64 of grid.shape[:-1].

Usage: a through hole is sdf_subtract(part, cylinder_sdf(...)) (make height longer than the part so no rim of the end faces remains). Bosses, pins and shafts use sdf_union. If an infinitely long cylinder is needed, make height large enough (once the end faces are outside the evaluated region, only the side matters).

The 3d op cylinder_sdf bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tunable parameters; neither a nor b is used.
